requirements_to_testpoints.stimulus: Power up with the supplied wiring and RTC initialization value 2024-11-24T04:48:00; allow successful startup acquisition.
requirements_to_testpoints.oracle: Serial initializes at 9600 baud and setup returns within 500 ms. Exactly one line is emitted: Current time: 2024/11/24 (Sunday) 4:48:0. SDA remains on A4, SCL on A5, power on 5V, and ground on GND.2.
requirements_to_testpoints.requirement_text:
# RTC module

## Project Description
This is a simple Arduino project that uses RTC module to get current time.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- RTC module

## Circuit Description
The RTC module is connected to the Arduino. The VCC pin is connected to 5V, the GND pin to gnd2, the SDA pin to A4, and the SCL pin to A5.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Initialize serial communication
2. Check if the RTC module can begin
3. Read current time with RTC module
4. Print to the serial monitor in the following format: "Current time: YYYY/M/D (Day of the week) H:M:S"

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. Correct day and time is printed in the serial monitor.

## Notes for Implementation
- No actions are required in the loop function.
- Day of the week is one of the "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday".
- Use RTClib to generate RTC_DS1307 object and read the value.
- RTC module has I2C interface.

## Variants
There may be variants with GND pin.

## Test Inputs
Test init value is: "2024-11-24T04:48:00"
Given circuit (must preserve wiring):
{
    "version": 1.0,
    "author": "Blind Author",
    "description": "Get the current time using an RTC sensor",
    "config": {
        "gnd_pin": "GND.2",
        "vcc_pin": "5V"
    },
    "parts": [
        {
            "id": "arduino uno1",
            "type": "wokwi-arduino-uno",
            "top": 0,
            "left": 20
        },
        {
            "id": "ds1307 real time clock module1307",
            "type": "wokwi-ds1307",
            "top": 250,
            "left": 220,
            "attrs": {
                "initTime": "2024-11-24T04:48:00"
            }
        }
    ],
    "connections": [
        [
            "arduino uno1:GND.2",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:GND",
            "black",
            [
                "v20",
                "*",
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:5V",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:5V",
            "red",
            [
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:A4",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:SDA",
            "green",
            [
                "v16",
                "h0",
                "*",
                "h-34"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:A5",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:SCL",
            "orange",
            [
                "v20",
                "*",
                "h-30"
            ]
        ]
    ]
}

requirements_to_testpoints.stimulus: Start with io_1=true and an acquired io_0 epoch. Continue controller steps with io_1=true, then vary io_0 and toggle io_1.
requirements_to_testpoints.oracle: The first step asserts serial_0_trigger and copies io_0 to serial_0_value_0. Every subsequent step has a false trigger and retains the originally captured epoch; no repeated report occurs.
